checks.sources_say: Customer email states 'Policy number: VER-1001'; Policy Schedule policy_id is VER-1001 with holder Claire Martin.
checks.evidence: Customer email signature block; Policy Schedule in claims system.

checks.sources_say: The incident is a whole-vehicle theft (police receipt: 'RECEIPT OF A THEFT COMPLAINT (vehicle theft)'), which is coverage C4 'Theft — theft of the whole insured vehicle'; C4 is listed in the Policy Schedule coverages for VER-1001.
checks.evidence: police_report.pdf (complaint type 'vehicle theft'); contract.pdf page 2 coverage table C4; Policy Schedule coverages include C4.

checks.sources_say: Police receipt states 'Date of the theft: 29/10/2026, between 21:00 and 23:45'.
Customer email received 2026-10-30 ('I filed a complaint at the police station this morning'); police receipt 'Complaint filed on: 30/10/2026 at 09:25'.
checks.evidence: Customer email header and body; police_report.pdf 'Complaint filed on' line.

checks.sources_say: No repair quote or invoice exists in the email or attachments because the whole vehicle was stolen, not damaged; under the contract 'For theft (C4), the amount of the claim is the market value of the vehicle' (Policy Schedule market value €14,000), so a repair cost of 0 is consistent and no source states any repair cost.
checks.evidence: police_report.pdf (theft of whole vehicle, no repair quote attached); contract.pdf page 2: 'For theft (C4), the amount of the claim is the market value of the vehicle'; Article 1 repair-cost definition requires a repair quote, which does not exist here.

checks.sources_say: The email and police receipt describe a theft by unknown persons; the policyholder is the victim, not at fault. No source indicates fault by Claire Martin.
checks.evidence: Customer email ('My car was stolen'); police_report.pdf (complainant declares theft; both keys kept by complainant).

checks.sources_say: No third party is mentioned anywhere: the email describes a street theft and the police receipt lists only the complainant; the playbook's referral rule (commercial vehicle of another driver) has no triggering facts.
checks.evidence: Customer email; police_report.pdf (no other party named); handler playbook rule requires 'the other driver' being a commercial vehicle, which the sources do not state.

checks.sources_say: No third party is identified in the email or the police receipt; the thief is unknown ('entered in the register of stolen vehicles').
checks.evidence: police_report.pdf (no suspect/other party named); customer email.

checks.sources_say: The only attachment is police_report.pdf, and it belongs to this policyholder and vehicle: complainant 'Claire Martin', vehicle 'Peugeot 208 (2021)', matching the Policy Schedule holder and vehicle. For C4 theft the contract requires exactly one document: 'Police report'.
checks.evidence: police_report.pdf header/complainant/vehicle lines; Policy Schedule (holder Claire Martin, Peugeot 208 2021); contract.pdf page 2 required-documents table, C4 Theft row: 'Police report'.

checks.sources_say: None of the Article 3 exclusions is present: no alcohol/drugs, the policyholder holds a licence since 2012-05-14 (valid), no racing, no intentional damage by the policyholder (she is the victim of theft), no wear/mechanical failure. The receipt even notes both keys kept by the complainant and signs of break-in.
checks.evidence: contract.pdf page 2 Article 3 exclusion list; police_report.pdf ('Keys: both keys kept by the complainant', 'Signs of break-in reported'); Policy Schedule licence_date 2012-05-14.

verdict.summary: All recorded facts match the customer email and police_report.pdf, C4 theft is covered in the Policy Schedule, the claim was reported within the 2-day theft deadline, the required police report was provided and belongs to this policyholder and vehicle, no exclusion or playbook referral rule applies, so the staged payment should be approved.
